Atmospheric pressure from elevation

Source: R/shared-physics.R
ef_air_pressure.Rd

Computes the mean atmospheric pressure \(P\) at a given elevation above sea level with the simplified ideal-gas relation of FAO-56 (standard atmosphere at 20 degrees Celsius). It is used when no measured or regionalised pressure is available, for example for the shortwave transmissivity, the air density and the reference evapotranspiration.

Usage

ef_air_pressure(elevation)

Arguments

elevation

Numeric. Elevation above sea level [m]. Must be finite and lower than 293 / 0.0065 = 45 076.92 m, where the base of the power law becomes non-positive. Negative elevations (below sea level) are allowed.

Value

A numeric vector of atmospheric pressure \(P\) [kPa] with the length of elevation. If elevation is a matrix or array, the result keeps its dim.

Details

The pressure is $$P = 101.3 \left(\frac{293 - 0.0065 z}{293}\right)^{5.26}$$ where \(z\) is elevation [m] and \(P\) is in kPa (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eq. 7).

Assumptions (FAO-56, chapter 3 and annex 3): standard atmosphere with a reference temperature of 293 K at sea level and a constant lapse rate of 0.0065 K m-1; the exponent 5.26 approximates \(g / (\alpha_1 R)\) with g = 9.807 m s-2, R = 287 J kg-1 K-1 and \(\alpha_1\) = 0.0065 K m-1. The result is a mean pressure for the site: synoptic pressure variations are not represented. FAO-56 states that the effect of pressure on evapotranspiration is small and that the mean value for a location is sufficient.

Missing values (NA, NaN) propagate to the output without errors or warnings. elevation must be numeric (double or integer) and non-empty. Infinite values or elevations of 45 076.92 m or more raise an error of class earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error). A plausible elevation range for a study area is not checked here (no threshold has a documented reference).

Verification status: VERIFICADA (identical to FAO-56, chapter 3, Eq. 7). Its attribution to ASCE-EWRI (2005) has not been verified.

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

See also

Other shared physical quantities: ef_latent_heat_vaporization()

Examples

# Sea level: 101.3 kPa
ef_air_pressure(0)
#> [1] 101.3

# Several elevations (m)
ef_air_pressure(c(0, 1000, 1800, 3000))
#> [1] 101.30000  90.02462  81.75580  70.51497
